The Pre-Launch Plan

February → April

Phase 1 · February

Plant the Seed
+ Build the World

Wk 1–2: Mystery · Wk 3–4: Identity

Build curiosity first — then define the vibe so deeply that people feel EILM before they've worn it. Waitlist goes live end of month.

  • Cryptic EILM logo — no caption, no context
  • "Everyone Is Looking At Me." — text only
  • Blurred product teaser — just a fabric glimpse
  • Founder POV video — "I've been building something"
  • Brand colour palette reveal — 6 colours only
  • Sydney streets moodboard
  • Brand voice post — what EILM is and isn't
  • "She lives in activewear 80% of the time." post
  • BTS photoshoot prep — Sydney location scouting
  • "The name EILM explained." Pin this.
  • Lifestyle moodboard: pilates → café → errands
  • "What does confidence feel like to you?"

Phase 2 · March

Show the Goods
+ Create Urgency

Wk 1–2: Reveals · Wk 3–4: Pre-orders

First product reveals — then the 72-hour pre-order window. Convert warm leads into buyers before public launch in April.

  • First full product reveal — hero piece, clean shot
  • Material deep-dive carousel — fabric & stitching
  • Waitlist officially open — push hard
  • Second product drop — full colourway showcase
  • Sydney photoshoot BTS reel
  • Movement test reel — Y-Zone seamless in action
  • Waitlist milestone — "X people already signed up"
  • Pre-orders LIVE — 72hrs waitlist only
  • Full collection carousel — every piece styled
  • "X pieces already pre-ordered." Social proof
  • Founder explains each product's backstory
  • Countdown reel — "X days until EILM launches"

Phase 3 · April ✦

Launch Day

Wk 1: Drop · Wk 2: Validate · Wk 3–4: Sustain

The moment three months of work was building to. Not launching to strangers — launching to a community that already feels ownership of the brand.

  • Launch day reel — cinematic, emotional
  • "We're live." Simple, confident, link in bio
  • Repost every single first customer photo
  • Lifestyle shoots — EILM around Sydney
  • Customer photos, testimonials, community love
  • Founder personal thank you post
  • "3 ways to wear your EILM set" styling reel
  • Restock announcement if sold out
  • May teaser — hint at what's next

Know the Market

Competitor Analysis

CSB
City Sports Babe
Aesthetic
Bold, colourful, high-impact. Very social-media-first. Influencer heavy.
Audience
18–28, gym culture, Australian-based, confidence-led but louder.
Weakness
Lacks quiet luxury angle. Not designed for tall frames. Generic sizing.
✦ EILM owns the "minimal over loud" space CSB leaves open. Tall girl fit as differentiator.
White Fox
Athleisure + Lifestyle
Aesthetic
Clean, soft, aspirational. Very lifestyle-driven. Beach meets gym.
Audience
Broad 18–35 demo. Very mainstream Australia. Massive reach.
Weakness
Trying to be everything to everyone. Lost niche credibility. Sizing inconsistent.
✦ EILM wins with hyper-specific audience vs. White Fox's broad net.
Sporty & Rich
Luxury Sportswear · USA
Aesthetic
Vintage-inspired, East Coast preppy. Muted palette, retro fonts. Editorial.
Audience
20–35, global, high purchasing power. Fashion-forward.
Weakness
Not performance-focused. US-centric. Out of reach for many in AU.
✦ EILM = the accessible Sporty & Rich for Australia — same energy, Sydney roots, actually wearable.

EILM vs. All Three

None design for tall girls. None have seamless Y-Zone tech. None sit at the NYC × Seoul × Sydney intersection EILM owns.

The White Space

Minimal aesthetic of S&R + performance of CSB + versatility of White Fox — made in Sydney, for tall girls, by someone who needed it herself.

Positioning

"EILM is the only Australian sportswear brand designed specifically for tall women who refuse to choose between looking good and performing well."

Why EILM Wins

Unique Selling Points

Seamless Y-Zone Legging

Strategically placed seamless zones eliminating camel toe, reducing friction, moving with the body. Not found anywhere else in the AU market at this price point.

Designed for Tall Girls

Not a factory template stretched to fit. Every cut, length and proportion engineered for 168cm+. Longer inseams. Higher rises that actually sit right. Finally.

Owner-Inspired Design

Every piece exists because the founder needed it and couldn't find it. Real frustration turned into real design. That authenticity is felt in every detail.

The EILM Difference

"Built by a tall girl, for tall girls, who are tired of settling."

CSB doesn't have this story. White Fox doesn't have this fit. Sporty & Rich doesn't have this price or this market. EILM owns a clear, defensible, deeply personal white space.
